# no-multiple-space-atx

- ID: `MD019`
- Category: Headings
- Default: on, severity warning
- Fixable: yes
- Tags: `headings`, `atx`, `spaces`

Only one space follows the \# marks that open a heading.

## Why

The extra spaces have no purpose, because they do not change the rendered
heading.

## Options

This rule has no options.

## Fix

The fix reduces the spaces to one. gomdlint may report a finding without a fix
when the fix would change a line with one character in brackets, such as \[x\]
or \[1\], or the lines around it up to a blank line, because it could add or
remove a task list checkbox.

## Example

This document breaks the rule:

```markdown
# Guide

##   Install

Run the installer.
```

gomdlint reports:

```text
3:4 Multiple spaces (3) after hash on ATX style heading
```

The fix changes it to:

```markdown
# Guide

## Install

Run the installer.
```

## Configure

Under `rules`, `no-multiple-space-atx: false` turns the rule off and
`no-multiple-space-atx: error` reports its findings as errors. The flag
`--disable no-multiple-space-atx` turns it off for one run.

## Silence one line

```markdown
<!-- markdownlint-disable-next-line no-multiple-space-atx -->
```
